prompt: A loan-approval model approves applicants from some neighborhoods far less often than equally qualified applicants elsewhere.
tells: far less often than equally qualified applicants
why: Similar people getting different outcomes by group is a fairness problem.
trap: Explaining the decision wouldn't fix the unequal outcomes.

prompt: A résumé-screening model trained on ten years of past hires ranks women lower for engineering roles.
tells: trained on ten years of past hires
why: Bias copied from historical data disadvantages a group: fairness.
trap: Inclusiveness is about designing for everyone's needs; this is unequal treatment in outcomes.

prompt: Before launch, the team compares error rates of a medical triage model separately for each age group and ethnicity.
tells: separately for each age group and ethnicity
why: Measuring performance by group is how you check fairness.
trap: Reliability checks whether it works in general; per-group comparison is the fairness check.

prompt: A pricing model quotes higher premiums to one group, even though claims history is the same as everyone else's.
why: Equal risk, unequal price: a fairness issue.
trap: Being open about the price doesn't make it fair.

prompt: A face-matching system has an error rate of 1% for lighter-skinned users and 8% for darker-skinned users.
tells: 1% for lighter-skinned users and 8% for darker-skinned users
why: Very different error rates between groups is a fairness problem.
trap: Overall reliability may look fine; the gap between groups is the issue.

prompt: To fix a model that underperforms for older patients, the team adds more data from patients over 70 and retrains.
tells: adds more data from patients over 70
why: Rebalancing training data to close a gap between groups is a fairness fix.
trap: The patients can use the system; it just treats them worse, which is fairness rather than inclusiveness.

prompt: A job-ad system shows high-paying roles mostly to men, because men clicked those ads more in the past.
why: Allocating opportunities unequally by group is a fairness harm.
trap: Past clicks explain the bias; they don't excuse it.

prompt: An image model asked for 'a CEO' almost always draws a middle-aged white man.
tells: almost always draws a middle-aged white man
why: Stereotyped outputs that underrepresent groups are a fairness issue in generative AI.
trap: Content filters block harmful content; stereotyping is a fairness concern.
